A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TRACED, with matching methods and retained experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original MiniGrid and BipedalWalker experiments, including generalization results, ablations, curriculum analyses, and training-time measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds multi-agent JaxNav evaluations and a Co-Learnability temporal-consistency experiment.

M1.justification: The scoring equations, Algorithm 1, transition-model architectures, and losses remain unchanged. The timing notes clarify signal availability; Appendix S's shadow agent is an analytical control, not a new TRACED component.

E1.justification: Appendices Q and S add training and evaluation on multi-agent JaxNav, extending coverage beyond MiniGrid navigation and BipedalWalker locomotion. The existing domains and PerfectMaze variants remain.

E2.justification: v3 explicitly excludes SFL. v4 adds a dedicated comparison against SFL and PLR⊥, identified as Robust PLR, on JaxNav (Appendix Q, Figure 22). The original benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new JaxNav comparison uses 4,550 PPO updates, CVaR across risk levels, and evaluation-set mean win rate. Appendix S introduces controlled shadow-agent replay to obtain aligned consecutive-step measurements. Existing MiniGrid and BipedalWalker protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix S adds a substantive test of whether Co-Learnability persists across consecutive steps, using cloned agents and forced replay of the same levels. This question was not directly tested in v3; its existing ablations and supplementary analyses remain.

E5.justification: v4 explicitly identifies all plot shading as 95% confidence intervals, reports three seeds for the new JaxNav studies, and adds Pearson and Spearman significance tests in Appendix S. Existing experiments' run counts and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 22 adds JaxNav results showing stronger CVaR than Robust PLR and performance comparable to SFL. Figure 21 adds PerfectMaze aggregate metrics; Appendix S reports Pearson correlation 0.3998 and Spearman correlation 0.2013. Existing Tables 1–15 retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Beyond v3's motivating regret decomposition, Appendix R introduces Lipschitz and loss-domination assumptions, a coupling-based transition-loss definition, a dynamics-mismatch lemma with proof, and a theorem claiming a tighter regret-approximation bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution and performance claims concerning ATPL, Co-Learnability, zero-shot generalization, curriculum complexity, and training efficiency.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the new JaxNav comparison as capturing learnability benefits without additional learnability evaluation, and the temporal analysis as showing mild persistence of Co-Learnability. It also frames ATPL as a theoretically principled correction. Appendix L's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies when difficulty and Co-Learnability estimates become usable and documents the shadow-agent cloning and replay procedure. Existing architecture, hardware, software, hyperparameter, and code-access information is retained; most JaxNav settings are referred to the cited SFL protocol.

R1.justification: Appendix J expands discussion of SFL and adds GoalGAN (Florensa et al., 2018) and ProCuRL (Tzannetos et al., 2023). The existing positioning against ACCEL and CENIE and the Co-Learnability novelty claim remain.

P1.justification: Localized additions explain signal timing, rank transformation, theoretical support, and the SFL comparison. Appendices Q–S are appended, while the main narrative, section order, and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures 21–23, adjusts Figure 7's axis labeling, and reflows existing figures and tables across pages. The established visual format and most existing displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The JaxNav comparison and temporal-consistency study address empirical gaps in v3, while Figure 21 improves result reporting. However, Appendix R.3 introduces an unsupported stronger guarantee: Lemma 1's upper bound does not justify the claimed smaller absolute-error bound simply by subtracting the ATPL correction. These empirical benefits coexist with a new theoretical overclaim, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
